subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should #43367 remain the canonical umbrella for multi-agent orchestration instability while focused fixes land, or should maintainers replace it with narrower canonical issues now that the config-write race is shipped?
rationale: The remaining work crosses session ownership, completion delivery guarantees, fallback cancellation, and product semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent contract from partial source fixes alone.

options.title: Keep umbrella canonical
options.body: Keep #43367 open, land focused slices such as #86540 only with proof, and use this issue to coordinate the remaining contract decisions.

options.title: Split into narrower canonicals
options.body: Close #43367 only after explicitly naming replacement canonical issues for session locks, completion delivery, fallback cancellation, and isolation semantics.

options.title: Close after one partial PR
options.body: Treat #86540 or the shipped config lock as sufficient and close the umbrella, accepting that other open production-evidence threads remain separate.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella canonical
recommendation.body: Keep #43367 open, land focused slices such as #86540 only with proof, and use this issue to coordinate the remaining contract decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing owner across subagent registry, session-lock, and product-boundary history.
